prs.title: feat(minsize): show exact byte counts in minsize.snap
prs.author: Dunqing
prs.body:
## Why

`tasks/minsize/minsize.snap` printed sizes with two decimals, so changes under 10 bytes (files under 1 MB) or under 10 KB (files over 1 MB) never showed up. For example, typescript.js is 3,311,949 bytes and could shrink by about 6.9 KB while still printing `3.31 MB`. A new optimization could save real bytes and still leave the snapshot unchanged.

## What

Oxc's minified and gzip columns are now exact byte counts:

```
10.95 MB    | 3,311,949 B | 3.49 MB     | 849,754 B   | 915.50 kB   |           4 | typescript.js
```

The values match the previous rounded ones, so the snapshot update here only changes formatting. The original-size and esbuild columns are unchanged. `tasks/minsize/README.md` notes the new format.

## Trade-offs

- Any PR that changes minifier output must now update `minsize.snap`, so stacked PRs will conflict on it more often. Re-running `cargo minsize` resolves the conflict.
- Exact gzip sizes depend on the `flate2` version, so a bump of that dependency may also need a snapshot update.

## Verification

- `CARGO_BUILD_WARNINGS=deny cargo clippy -p oxc_minsize --all-targets` passes, with and without `--all-features`.
- `cargo minsize` regenerates a snapshot whose numbers equal the exact sizes of the minified outputs it writes to `target/minifier/`.

prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Remove the `comment_meta` field from `Lanes`.

It's not used internally in `oxc_lexer`, and its unclear what utility it'd have outside of the crate (e.g. in parser).

If I'm wrong, and it would be useful to the parser, it'd be simple to bring it back later on. IMO we should ideally expose as little as possible initially, and only add to the API once it's clear we need them.

prs.title: refactor(lexer): simplify creating comments
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Refactor of comments-related code.

Simplify creating comments by:

- Pass `CommentKind` directly into `push_comment_record`.
- Pass `followed_by_newline` directly into `push_comment_record`. Only one call site needs the loop to search for a trailing newline, so move it to that call site.

prs.title: refactor(lexer): remove multiline flag from comment flags
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Refactor.

After #28311, comment "meta" flags are no longer part of the external API. Simplify the remaining code to not pack the comment content byte and the multiline flag into a single byte. Multiline flag is only relevant in `lex_block_comment` so just track that state locally there.

This clears the way for the next PR #28314.

prs.title: refactor(lexer): comments classification produce `CommentContent` directly
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Refactor.

Comment content had 2 different representations - a set of constants in `oxc_lexer` (`CONTENT_LEGAL` etc), and the existing `CommentContent` enum from `oxc_ast`. `classify` returned the former, and then it was converted later to `CommentContent`.

Simplify by removing the other representation, and making `classify` just return `CommentContent` directly. This removes some instructions, but main motivation is just to simplify the code.

prs.title: fix(coverage): clone missing submodules once
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
- Check all required coverage fixture roots before `TestData::load` starts its parallel suite loaders.
- Run `just submodules` once when any required suite is empty.
- Keep `runtime` test262-only by checking only its test262 root.

This prevents a fresh checkout from launching one `just submodules` process per missing suite.

prs.title: fix(ast): prevent greyed out fields in AST types in IDEs
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body: At some point Rust Analyzer started greying out the fields of AST structs in VS Code due to a strange interaction with the `#[ast]` macro. Fix this by making the macro add an `#[allow(rust_analyzer::inactive_code)]` attribute to struct fields.

prs.title: perf(ast): reduce compile time of `#[ast]` macro
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Improve the compile time of `oxc_ast` crate by making the `#[ast]` proc macro faster.

Instead of using `parse_quote!` to generate attributes, generate them by hand as token trees and clone them. This avoids the overhead of lexing and parsing when expanding the macro.

`oxc_ast` crate is one of the "deepest" crates so many other crates compilation is queued up behind it. We want the `#[ast]` macro to be as low overhead as possible.

prs.title: perf(str): `static_ident!` and `static_str!` macros guarantee const evaluation
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
`static_ident!` and `static_str!` macros are intended to evaluate at compile time. This is especially valuable for `static_ident!` as we want the hash to be calculated at compile time.

Wrap both in a `const { ... }` block to ensure they are const-evaluated.

prs.title: perf(linter/plugins): create AST nodes with `Object.create` instead of `__proto__` literals
prs.author: wan9chi
prs.body:
## Summary

oxlint's raw transfer deserializer creates every AST node as an object literal with `__proto__: NodeProto` (for the lazy `loc` getter). V8 creates such object literals on a slow path: it builds a plain object, then changes its prototype with a runtime call.

This PR changes the raw transfer codegen (`LocFieldAdder` in `tasks/ast_tools/src/generators/raw_transfer.rs`) to create nodes with `Object.create(NodeProto)` followed by property assignments:

```js
// `main`
node = (parent = { __proto__: NodeProto, type: "CallExpression", callee: null, /* ... */ });

// This PR
node = (parent = (node$0 = Object.create(NodeProto), node$0.type = "CallExpression", node$0.callee = null, /* ... */ node$0));
```

Nodes keep the same prototype, own properties, property order and attributes. `napi/parser`'s deserializers are unaffected.

## Benchmark

Deserialization time when linting [vscode](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode) @ `3db52ff` (15,122 files, 53.4M AST nodes) with a single JS rule which visits `DebuggerStatement` (to make sure deserialization isn't eliminated as dead code). Apple M4 Pro, Node 26.5.0, release build.

Measured by timing each [`deserializeProgramOnly` call in `initAst`](apps/oxlint/src-js/plugins/source_code.ts#L86) with `performance.now()` (local instrumentation, not part of this PR), summed over all 15,086 deserialized files. Medians of 5 interleaved runs, after a warmup run.

| | Deserialize |
|---|--:|
| `main` | 4.49 s |
| This PR | 0.91 s (**4.9×**

prs.title: perf(linter/import/no-cycle): don't allocate paths already seen
prs.author: camchenry
prs.body:
We always allocate (by `.clone()`) a new path, even just for checking membership. Instead, we use borrowed data for the membership check and then only clone a new path when we insert new data, dramatically reducing allocations needed.

Running on `vscode`:

Metric | Before | After | Change
-- | -- | -- | --
`no-cycle` allocations | 33,072,678 | 19,051,530 | −42.4%
`no-cycle` allocated bytes | 2.738 GB | 1.700 GB | −37.9%
